purpose: Declared, exhaustive difference list for the Codex variant of the msg GUI (DEV-CX-014, approved-translation). The Claude board stays byte-identical to the canonical one; the Codex variant differs from it by exactly the substitutions below plus mechanical invocation-token translation (DEV-CX-001). Anything else is drift and fails the eval.

human_gates.why: A board-launched run must be able to stop on a mandatory human gate, show the question, and continue with the answer the person chose. Neither runner can do that through a one-shot pipe, so the server owns the channel and both runtimes bind the same one — the board UX is identical on Claude and Codex, and neither side may answer a gate for the user.
human_gates.seam: $MSG_GUI_GATE_DIR/<gate-id>.ask.json is written by the run; $MSG_GUI_GATE_DIR/<gate-id>.answer is written by the server with the chosen option label (or the declared default, on an explicit dismissal). Both writers rename a .tmp file into place. There is no timeout and no auto-answer on the server side.
human_gates.codex_binding: .agents/scripts/script-codex-gate.sh (codex/gate-template.sh) writes the ask file and blocks on the answer file whenever MSG_GUI_GATE_DIR is set, emitting GATE_CHANNEL=gui alongside the existing awaiting-answer envelope; MSG_GUI_GATE_TIMEOUT bounds the wait and blocks rather than defaulting.
human_gates.claude_binding: residual — `claude -p` cannot hold an AskUserQuestion open. The interception path is live-verified (Claude Agent SDK canUseTool returning allow + an `answers` map, per evals/codex/lib/claude-session.mjs), and the driver contract is recorded in server.py; a board driver that binds this seam has not yet been built or run.
human_gates.variant_impact: none — the gate surface is server-side and runtime-neutral, so it adds no Codex-only substitution to the board.

substitutions.why: Every occurrence is the console naming the active runtime in visible copy: the prompt placeholder and the six ask/fix quick-action buttons. The board names the runtime the user is actually talking to.
